Here's the summary of what was built:

**`output_model_new.py`** contains two AveLang kernels for depthwise 3×3 convolution (groups=in_channels):

- **`depthwise_conv2d_tiled_kernel`** — the optimized fast path. Each block handles one (batch, channel) pair on a 16×16 output tile. The 18×18 input tile is loaded cooperatively into shared memory via `al.make_shared`, cutting global reads from ~18 per output element down to ~1.3. A 3D grid `(W_tiles, H_tiles, B×C)` covers all output positions. Used when stride=1 and padding=0 (the eval test case).

- **`depthwise_conv2d_simple_kernel`** — the general fallback. One thread per output element, direct global reads, handles arbitrary stride/padding/bias. Used for non-unit stride or when padding is nonzero.

**Results on MI300X (gfx942, BF16):**
| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Compiled | true |
| Correctness | 5/5 trials |
| Runtime | 7.32 ms (mean) |
| Ref runtime | 8.40 ms (mean) |
| Speedup | ~13% over reference |
